source_title: Ancient Egyptian Mythology: bounded New Kingdom witnesses
continuity_scope: Papyrus Chester Beatty I, The Contendings of Horus and Seth (Ramesside; recto pages 1–16) and the Papyrus of Ani, Book of the Dead Spell 125/Judgment vignette (19th Dynasty, c. 1250 BCE). The two witnesses are not treated as one timeless or universal Egyptian theology.
work_or_witnesses: A. H. Gardiner, The Library of A. Chester Beatty: Description of a Hieratic Papyrus with a Mythological Story, Love-Songs, and Other Miscellaneous Texts (1931), Papyrus Chester Beatty I, recto pp. 1–16.
Papyrus of Ani, British Museum EA10470 frame 3, Book of the Dead Spell 125/Judgment vignette; UCL Digital Egypt provides a comparative Spell 125 text from Papyrus of Nu.
coverage_rule: All individually named major agents who act or rule in the Contendings, plus Ani and major named divine/judgment agents materially represented in Ani’s Spell 125 frame. Exclude the formulaic forty-two assessors, unnamed divine councils, and deities/episodes only in other periods or local corpora.
omissions: Pyramid Texts, Coffin Texts, other Book of the Dead spells, local temple theologies, and later Greco-Roman synthesis are outside scope.
The forty-two Spell 125 assessors are a formulaic collective, not individual nodes in this bounded pass.
No historical claim is made that Contendings’ succession drama is a direct record of political history.
uncertainties: Egyptian divine names, kinship, forms, and offices vary materially by period, locale, manuscript, and genre.
Ani frame 3 combines Spell 30B wording and judgment imagery; UCL’s full Spell 125 text is from Nu, not Ani, and is used only as a comparative spell locator.
The Chester Beatty narrative is a Ramesside witness, not a synthesis of all Horus–Seth traditions.
evidence_basis: Museum object documentation, UCL university teaching text, and Gardiner’s critical publication/Chester Beatty witness; citations retain witness/page/spell-frame distinctions.
